label: Hero
purpose: The first photograph anyone sees. One frame, wide and cinematic, with quiet space on the left for copy.

label: Categories
purpose: One frame per body style. Each tile is the front door to its own part of the marketplace and has to earn the click on photography alone.

label: Dealers
purpose: Exterior cover photography for dealer profiles, and the fallback mark a dealership wears until it uploads its own.

label: Showrooms
purpose: Interior architecture. Used where a dealer profile needs to feel like a building you have walked into rather than a page you have loaded.

label: Lifestyle
purpose: People, and the part of their life a car is in. Used wherever the product needs to be about a person rather than a vehicle — and where a stock model would undo the whole effect.

label: Places
purpose: Where Surf4Cars is. Cape Town and the Western Cape — the identity set that makes a South African marketplace look like one instead of like anywhere.

label: Backgrounds
purpose: Full-bleed editorial plates behind long-form sections. Judged on how much quiet area they hold, not on their subject.

label: Promotions
purpose: Photographic plates for promotional banners. SURF typography is composed over the approved plate in the layout — never burned into the pixels.

label: Manufacturers
purpose: Marque logos. A manufacturer's mark is its trademark: it is supplied under licence or not used at all, and can never be substituted from a stock library.

label: Vehicles
purpose: Photography of individual cars for sale, published by the dealer who owns the vehicle. A listing's photographs are a factual claim about that car, so a stock frame here would be a misrepresentation.
